For Petitioner : Mr.K.P.S.Palanivel Rajan  Senior Counsel  for Mr.S.Vijayakumar  For R1 : Mr.K.Govindharajan,
 Deputy Solicitor General  For RR2, 3 and 5 : Mr.K.Balasubramani  Special Government Pleader  For R4 : Mr.K.Seemaraj  ORDER

This writ petition has been filed challenging the G.O.Ms.No.187, Agricultural (AA2) Department,
dated 27.07.2017, in and by which, the second respondent accorded saction of prosecution against the petitioner.

2. The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Department has registered a case against the petitioner in Crime No.1 of 2012 that while he was working as Seed Certification Officer, he had created false records, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis forged the signatures, prepared false inspection reports as if 22 farmers had raised Vamban-3 black gram seed farms and he had visited those farms twice, taken seed samples from those farmers and also sanctioned a sum of Rs.2,40,471/- to those fake seed farmers.

The case in Crime No.1 of 2012 was registered for the offences under Sections 167, 409, 420, 468, 471, 477A of IPC and under Section 13(1)(c) and (d) read with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
The Investigation Agency, after collecting the evidence, has made a request to the Government for sanction of prosecution as required under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The Government, after considering the request and the evidence placed by the Vigilance and Anti-corruption Department, accorded sanction vide G.O.(Ms)No.187, Agriculture (AA2) Department dated 27.07.2017, which is under challenge in this writ petition.
3. This Court has entertained this writ petition on 25.11.2022 by issuing notice to the respondents.

Though this Court has not granted any interim order, it appears that by referring this writ petition,
the trial in Spl.C.C.No.4 of 2017 is kept pending without even framing the charges for the past seven years.

The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, by referring the Government Order,
submits that the second respondent has accorded sanction without any application of mind.
After elaborate arguments, the learned Senior Counsel seeks permission of this court to withdraw this writ petition.
An endorsement is also made to that effect.

5. The learned Special Government Pleader has produced a diary extract of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Tuticorin, in Spl.C.C.No.4 of 2017 and submits that in view of the pendency of the writ petition as against the sanction order, the trial in Spl.S.C.No.4 of 2017 is still kept pending.

6. Though the learned Senior Counsel seeks permission of this Court to withdraw this writ petition filed by the petitioner challenging the sanction order, this Court takes note of the fact that though the case in Crime No.1 of 2012 was registered in the year 2012, the final report was filed only in the year 2017.
Though this Court has not granted any interim order in the writ petition, the trial is kept pending at the stage of framing of charges.

From the date of registration of this case, i.e. for the past 11 years, there is no https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis progress in the criminal case, which has been registered for the allegation of corruption.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to dismiss this writ petition as withdrawn.
7. This type of delay in dealing with the corruption cases, in fact, is one of the reasons for the increase in corruption in this State.

It is not only the responsibility of the Vigilance and Anti-corruption Department and the Courts are also having certain responsibilities in concluding the cases in a time bound manner.
8.

Accordingly, this writ petition is dismissed with a direction to the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Thoothukudi, to conduct the trial in Spl.C.C.No.4 of 2017 on day-to-day basis and dispose of the case within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petiton is closed.
